name: Harness, context, sub-agents and recursion ranked
purpose: Harnesses are ranked by cost and time at the same pass rate, across the context given to them and their use of sub-agents and recursion.
record: A balanced score of pass rate, cost and time for each setting, on the same cases.
cascading_conditionals: idea [kind=idea | scale=esoi/idea-rating-scale.md | min-pass-rate=0.75 | when=a new alternative is described: rate its description on the five questions of the scale before it is built] > offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=hubofhubs/the_world/tools/delegated_agent_sessions/tests/test_deep_session_subagents.py passes] > public [real=no | when=the arm has an unexpired prior of grade C or better in public_priors.csv beside the solution, set by the prior rule of docs/explanation/public-evidence.md (direct or borrowed from a published live-benchmark row, never estimated); a prior orders unmeasured arms and never outranks a measured result] > one [sample=sample:1 | real=yes | gate=all-pass | when=a single real deep session runs end to end and is hand-read] > measured [real=yes | gate=competitive | max-age-days=90 | when=a call budget is set and the spend is approved]

name: Open-ended work finished per cost and time (agent sessions)
purpose: An arm (an agent harness, the provider it drives and a tier) is ranked by how much open-ended work it finishes correctly, for what it costs and how long it takes, on the same cases as every other arm.
record: The balanced score of [balance.agent_sessions] in esoi.toml (pass rate, cost per case and seconds per case, with the weights and budgets stated there), per arm, over evaluation/agent_sessions: read-and-report tasks, coding tasks checked by their own tests (restored by the harness before the check) and milestone-shaped deliverables checked by a written rubric (a video script, research that cites its source files, a dated plan from notes). Every run is recorded, partial ones included, with calls, cost and seconds.
disadvantages: Eighteen cases written by one author cannot separate close arms; the deliverables are judged by rubric terms, not by how well they read; the research case uses local sources, not the live web; Claude Code dollars are the CLI's list-price estimate on a flat subscription; public problems may be known to the model.
cascading_conditionals: idea [kind=idea | scale=esoi/idea-rating-scale.md | min-pass-rate=0.75 | when=a new arm (harness, provider, tier) is described: its five ratings and reasons are a row of arm_ideas.csv beside the solution, rated before it is built] > offline [real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the harness's own tests pass with no model: test_headless_runner.py replays each harness's recorded event stream through a fake program (report, tokens, cost, launch failure, time limit, cancel, escalation), and the Claude Code runner tests pass; the none arm is the zero bound] > public [real=no | when=the arm has an unexpired prior of grade C or better in public_priors.csv beside the solution, set by the prior rule of docs/explanation/public-evidence.md (direct or borrowed from a published live-benchmark row, never estimated); a prior orders unmeasured arms and never outranks a measured result] > one [sample=sample:1 | real=yes | gate=all-pass | when=the offline stage passed for the harness and the arm's provider has credentials where we measure: one real case runs end to end and its report is read by hand] > staged [sample=sample:6 | real=yes | gate=competitive | max-age-days=90 | when=the one case passed and a call budget is set with --max-calls: two cases of each kind] > whole [sample=full | real=yes | max-age-days=90 | when=the staged sample passed its gate, or did not separate the leading arms]
